abstract: We apply our recent Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm [1] to the combinatorial problem of bounded occurrence Max E3LIN2. The input is a set of linear equations each of which contains exactly three boolean variables and each equation says that the sum of the variables mod 2 is 0 or is 1. Every variable is in no more than $D$ equations. A random string will satisfy 1/2 of the equations. We show that the level one QAOA will efficiently produce a string that satisfies $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{101D^{1/2}\,ln\,D}\right)$ times the number of equations. A recent classical algorithm [5, 6] achieved $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{constant}{D^{1/2}}\right)$. We also show that in the typical case the quantum computer will output a string that satisfies $\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3e}\,D^{1/2}}\right)$ times the number of equations.

specification.problem: Bounded-occurrence Max E3LIN2: given linear equations over GF(2), each with exactly three boolean variables and right-hand side 0 or 1, with each variable in at most D equations, find a string satisfying as many equations as possible using level-one QAOA.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Problem definition and the stated approximation guarantees only. Circuit-level QAOA details (cost Hamiltonian, mixer, angles) are not given in the abstract; any such detail would be standard background or assumption.

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over all n-bit strings (|+>^{\otimes n}), the standard QAOA start state (assumed, not in abstract)

steps.description: Prepare |+>^n on the variable register (standard QAOA background).
Apply level-one (p=1) phase-separation unitary from the cost Hamiltonian encoding the equations, with an angle gamma (assumed standard form; not in abstract).
Apply the p=1 mixing unitary with transverse-field angle beta (assumed standard); angles are chosen so the expected satisfied fraction exceeds the 1/2 random baseline.

specification.measurement: Measure all n qubits in the computational basis to obtain a candidate string z (standard QAOA readout, assumed). Repeat as needed; the abstract's guarantees concern the satisfied fraction of the output string.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate the number of satisfied equations for each sampled z classically and keep the best string. Sampling count and any high-probability argument are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Level-one QAOA uses the standard form: uniform start, one cost layer, one mixer layer, with one qubit per variable.
Computational-basis measurement with classical evaluation of satisfied equations is assumed.
